item.title: @wallstengine: OURA IPO IS ~4X OVERSUBSCRIBED Smart ring maker Oura’s IPO has received roughly four times as many...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OURA IPO IS ~4X OVERSUBSCRIBED
Smart ring maker Oura’s IPO has received roughly four times as many orders as shares available, per Bloomberg, with banks expected to stop taking orders Monday afternoon.
Oura and existing shareholders are offering 50M shares at $40-$44 each, raising up to $2.2B. Of that, Oura itself is selling 13.5M shares, while existing holders including Forerunner Ventures and Lifeline Ventures are selling 36.5M.
At the top of the range, Oura would carry a ~$14.1B market value and roughly $15B fully diluted valuation.
The IPO is expected to price Sept. 29, with shares set to trade on Nasdaq under $OURA.
The deal could also become the first U.S. IPO to raise more than $1B since July, despite several recent listings being postponed amid weaker market conditions.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: SOLIDIGM EYES $150B IPO SK Hynix is considering taking its U.S. storage subsidiary Solidigm public...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SOLIDIGM EYES $150B IPO
SK Hynix is considering taking its U.S. storage subsidiary Solidigm public as early as 2027 in an IPO that could raise about $15B and value the company at up to $150B, per Reuters.
Solidigm was created after SK Hynix acquired Intel’s NAND memory and SSD business for roughly $9B and combined those operations into a standalone U.S. subsidiary.
The company sells enterprise SSDs used in servers, cloud infrastructure and AI data centers, with a growing focus on high-capacity storage for AI workloads.
Solidigm has already begun meeting with investment banks for potential IPO roles, marking an early step toward a listing that could become the largest-ever U.S. semiconductor IPO.
SK Hynix has also been exploring ways to expand Solidigm, including a possible U.S. NAND manufacturing plant, with upstate New York reportedly under consideration.
Source: Reuters

The company sells enterprise SSDs used in servers, cloud infrastructure and AI data centers, with a growing focus on high-capacity storage for AI workloads.

Solidigm has already begun meeting with investment banks for potential IPO roles, marking an early step toward a listing that could become the largest-ever U.S. semiconductor IPO.

SK Hynix has also been exploring ways to expand Solidigm, including a possible U.S. NAND manufacturing plant, with upstate New York reportedly under consideration.

Source: Reuters

item.title: @wallstengine: Satya Nadella wants to bring Autopilot, Microsoft’s AI “chief of staff,” into your personal life: “...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Satya Nadella wants to bring Autopilot, Microsoft’s AI “chief of staff,” into your personal life:
“Autopilot should also go to the consumer side.”
Built on a hardened version of OpenClaw, it is designed to keep working continuously on tasks you delegate:
“You can give this Autopilot an identity, a computer and a workspace and some direction, and it goes off and has memory, and it’ll work on a continuous basis.”
At work, that could mean an agent managing invoices while you interact with it through Teams like another colleague. Nadella says Microsoft has spent the past four or five months hardening the sandbox and building out security and governance.
For consumers, he says trust will be just as important:
“The day you suddenly have your consumer agent do things that you never expected it is the day you stop using it.”
He also sees consumer agents potentially cutting out today’s middlemen, while enterprise agents could create a market bigger than cloud “by orders of magnitude.”
Source: Sources / @alexeheath
item.content:encoded:
Satya Nadella wants to bring Autopilot, Microsoft’s AI “chief of staff,” into your personal life:

“Autopilot should also go to the consumer side.”

Built on a hardened version of OpenClaw, it is designed to keep working continuously on tasks you delegate:

“You can give this Autopilot an identity, a computer and a workspace and some direction, and it goes off and has memory, and it’ll work on a continuous basis.”

At work, that could mean an agent managing invoices while you interact with it through Teams like another colleague. Nadella says Microsoft has spent the past four or five months hardening the sandbox and building out security and governance.

For consumers, he says trust will be just as important:

“The day you suddenly have your consumer agent do things that you never expected it is the day you stop using it.”

He also sees consumer agents potentially cutting out today’s middlemen, while enterprise agents could create a market bigger than cloud “by orders of magnitude.”

Source: Sources / @alexeheath

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The S&P 500 rises on reports that talks between the US and Iran have entered a "technical...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The S&P 500 rises on reports that talks between the US and Iran have entered a "technical stage," per Al Jazeera.
Details include:
1. Negotiations in New York have reportedly moved beyond initial diplomatic contacts into a "more detailed technical phase"
2. Technical experts joined the discussions in New York after a first meeting involving US envoys Witkoff and Kushner
3. Iran's proposed 7-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US ends its blockade is being discussed as an accelerated version of a previously discussed 60-day process
4. Both sides also continue to discuss other arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz
Oil prices are pulling back on the news.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The average sales price for a new single-family home fell -$47,700 MoM in August, or -9.1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The average sales price for a new single-family home fell -$47,700 MoM in August, or -9.1%, to $478,700, the largest monthly drop on record.
This is the lowest level since August 2024 and the 2nd-lowest level since September 2021.
The decline was driven by a shift toward lower-priced homes, as builders cut prices and offered incentives to clear inventory.
This comes as sales of homes under $300,000 rose to 22% of total sales last month from 19%, while sales of homes priced at $1 million+ fell to 4% from 6%.
As a result, total new home sales jumped +6.4% MoM, to 684,000, their highest since December 2025.
Meanwhile, median sales price fell -$24,200 YoY, or -5.8%, to $393,700, the 2nd-lowest reading since July 2021.
US home prices are falling to keep sales alive.

Set your MIN and MAX by asset class first. Add and trim in 50-150 bps increments, never a full position in one move. Longs bigger than shorts. Size inversely to volatility.
And remember what the max is actually for. Not to cap your upside - to make sure one bad position never needs a miracle to recover.

“What the current situation needs is technology.”

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The last time US Treasury yields were this high, total US national debt stood at just $8.9 trillion...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The last time US Treasury yields were this high, total US national debt stood at just $8.9 trillion.
Today, US debt stands at $40.1 trillion. That's +$31.2 trillion more, or over 4.5 TIMES higher.
This means every 1 percentage point in the average cost of servicing the debt now translates to ~$401 billion per year in interest expense.
In 2007, the same 1 percentage point translated to just ~$89 billion.
That’s an additional ~$312 BILLION in annual interest expense for every percentage point increase in borrowing cost.
This is a vastly different situation than it was 19 years ago.
The bond market matters more now than ever.

item.title: @wallstengine: $TSLA RAMPS OPTIMUS PRODUCTION 10X Tesla has increased Optimus output from a few dozen units per we...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$TSLA RAMPS OPTIMUS PRODUCTION 10X
Tesla has increased Optimus output from a few dozen units per week in Q2 to several 100, with managers targeting 1,000+ per week by year-end.
But the scale-up is still running into manufacturing problems, especially with Optimus’ hands, per The Information.
The hand and forearm contain 100+ screws and small components that still require manual assembly, while touch sensors and automated production equipment have faced reliability issues.
Tesla is also dealing with supplier constraints as some vendors struggle to maintain component quality at higher volumes.
On the AI side, Optimus still relies heavily on task-specific training. Tesla has collected 500,000+ hours of training data and aims to double that by year-end.
The current Optimus V3 units are mainly being used internally for testing, training and data collection and are not yet the final commercial version. Tesla plans to initially lease robots to outside customers, using real-world deployment data to improve the system over time.
Source: The Information
item.content:encoded:
$TSLA RAMPS OPTIMUS PRODUCTION 10X

Tesla has increased Optimus output from a few dozen units per week in Q2 to several 100, with managers targeting 1,000+ per week by year-end.

But the scale-up is still running into manufacturing problems, especially with Optimus’ hands, per The Information.

The hand and forearm contain 100+ screws and small components that still require manual assembly, while touch sensors and automated production equipment have faced reliability issues.

Tesla is also dealing with supplier constraints as some vendors struggle to maintain component quality at higher volumes.

On the AI side, Optimus still relies heavily on task-specific training. Tesla has collected 500,000+ hours of training data and aims to double that by year-end.

The current Optimus V3 units are mainly being used internally for testing, training and data collection and are not yet the final commercial version. Tesla plans to initially lease robots to outside customers, using real-world deployment data to improve the system over time.

Source: The Information

item.title: @wallstengine: $CIFR EXTENDS BARBER LAKE DEAL TO 20YRS Cipher Digital extended the contracted life of its Barber L...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$CIFR EXTENDS BARBER LAKE DEAL TO 20YRS
Cipher Digital extended the contracted life of its Barber Lake data center from 10 to 20 years, increasing total contracted revenue from $3.8B to more than $9B.
The structure combines its existing Fluidstack lease with a binding 10-year follow-on commitment from an unnamed AI lab, adding about $5.2B of incremental contracted revenue.
Data halls are expected to come online in phases from Q4 2026 through Q1 2027, with rent starting as each hall is delivered.
Cipher will absorb the first $359.3M of cost overruns above the original budget, while the tenant will reimburse 50% of costs above that threshold through additional rent over the lease term.

The Fed is working on a proposal that could raise its highest enhanced-oversight threshold from $700B to around $960B and move some additional requirements currently triggered near $100B closer to $150B, per Reuters.

Tesla was also selected as the primary supplier for ZET SCALE’s initial 2,500-truck order, while Einride recently ordered 500 Semis.
The long-range Semi is rated for ~500 miles, and Tesla says fleet operations have shown 98% uptime.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The average interest rate on a 30Y mortgage is up to 7.45%, its highest level in 3 years. This offi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The average interest rate on a 30Y mortgage is up to 7.45%, its highest level in 3 years.
This officially pushes the payment on a $500,000 mortgage to $3,479/month.
By comparison, the same mortgage came with a payment of $2,995/month just 7 months ago.
That's an additional $5,813/year in mortgage interest expense for homebuyers.
Mortgage rates are now up +150 basis points since late-February.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC SEEKS FOUNDER CONTROL AHEAD OF IPO Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a new stru...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC SEEKS FOUNDER CONTROL AHEAD OF IPO
Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a new structure that would give CEO Dario Amodei and the company’s six other co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power on most corporate matters, per The Information.
The founders would hold the special voting shares through a separate LLC, allowing them to retain control despite relatively small economic stakes. Dario Amodei currently owns about 2%.
One major exception: Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust would continue to control the appointment of most board members, while the founders’ board seats would increase from 2 to 3.
Employees are also expected to receive a special class of stock that could serve as tie-breaker votes on certain issues.
Anthropic, valued at $965B in May, is reportedly targeting at least a $1.5T valuation in an IPO now expected around late October or November.
Source: The Information

Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a new structure that would give CEO Dario Amodei and the company’s six other co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power on most corporate matters, per The Information.

One major exception: Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust would continue to control the appointment of most board members, while the founders’ board seats would increase from 2 to 3.

Employees are also expected to receive a special class of stock that could serve as tie-breaker votes on certain issues.

Anthropic, valued at $965B in May, is reportedly targeting at least a $1.5T valuation in an IPO now expected around late October or November.

Source: The Information

item.title: @WatcherGuru: Bitget says ~$351.6 million was drained from some of its hot wallets and that its cold wallets rema...
item.dc:creator: @WatcherGuru
item.description:
Bitget says ~$351.6 million was drained from some of its hot wallets and that its cold wallets remain secure.
The exchange also said user funds are safe and the full loss is covered by its "User Protection Fund," which holds ~$464 million for incidents like these.
Withdrawals are temporarily paused as the exchange completes a security review, while deposits and trading continue.
Bitget says law enforcement and on-chain security firms have been notified and will issue a full incident report within 24 hours.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Institutional investors bought +$4.1 billion in US equities in the week ending September 18th.
This marks their 3rd weekly purchase over the last 4 weeks.
As a result, the 4-week average of institutional purchases rose to +$2.9 billion.
At the same time, hedge funds purchased +$1.2 billion, bringing their 4-week average of purchases up to +$1.6 billion.
Meanwhile, retail investors sold -$2.2 billion last week, posting their 8th consecutive weekly sale.
Retail investors have now sold an average of -$1.9 billion in US equities per week over the last 4 weeks.
Institutions are buying while retail is selling.

BLUE ORIGIN RAISES $10B AT $140B VALUATION
Jeff Bezos has now invested roughly $30B into Blue Origin since founding the company in 2000, including another $2B as part of its first outside funding round.
Internal projections show revenue rising from: 2025: ~$800M 2026: ~$1.4B 2030: $30B+
Blue Origin expects growth to come from New Glenn launches, a planned satellite communications business and a future fleet of AI satellites.
The company currently employs ~15,000 people and is rebuilding its Florida launch complex after a New Glenn vehicle exploded on the launchpad in May.
Source: WSJ

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC SIGNS $11.6B AKAMAI CLOUD DEAL Anthropic has committed $11.6B over seven years to use Aka...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC SIGNS $11.6B AKAMAI CLOUD DEAL
Anthropic has committed $11.6B over seven years to use Akamai $AKAM infrastructure for growing CPU workloads, with options to expand the relationship by another $9B, bringing the potential total to ~$20B.
As part of the deal, Anthropic received warrants that could give it up to ~5% of Akamai. About 2% is expected to vest with the initial commitment, with the remaining 3% tied to further cloud spending.
Akamai expects ~$5.5B of capex related to the initial deal, including an additional ~$1.7B in 2026 to secure components such as memory.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The S&P Global US Composite PMI index jumped +2.4 points in September, to 58.4, its highe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The S&P Global US Composite PMI index jumped +2.4 points in September, to 58.4, its highest reading since July 2021.
This also marks the 4th consecutive monthly improvement in growth.
This was driven by the services sector, with its index rising +2.2 points, to 58.7, its highest level since October 2021.
At the same time, Manufacturing PMI surged +3.1 points, to 57.0, its highest since May 2022.
Excluding the post-2020 pandemic reopening surge in demand, the latest improvement in business activity is the strongest since 2015.
However, this growth comes amid severe supply chain bottlenecks and labor shortages, pushing backlogs sharply higher and adding to inflationary pressures.
Inflationary pressures are mounting.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META LAUNCHES AI GAME-BUILDING TOOLS Meta is launching Horizon Create and Horizon Studio, letting...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META LAUNCHES AI GAME-BUILDING TOOLS
Meta is launching Horizon Create and Horizon Studio, letting users build complete 2D or 3D games from AI prompts on mobile or in a browser.
Games can then be published across Facebook and Instagram, where users can jump from a clip directly into a multiplayer session without downloading a separate app.
Meta says the tools can generate gameplay systems, difficulty, art direction and multiplayer features, while still letting creators manually refine the experience.
The rollout is part of Meta’s broader shift to make Horizon a mobile-first platform rather than primarily a VR product.

item.title: @aliansarinik: Today we’re launching micro1’s PII transformation model, flow-transform 1.0, delivering frontier-le...
item.dc:creator: @aliansarinik
item.description:
Today we’re launching micro1’s PII transformation model, flow-transform 1.0, delivering frontier-level performance across detection, identity synthesis, and transformation of personally identifiable information.
On PrivacyBench, our model reaches 96.0% F1, outperforming every detection baseline we tested, including Tonic Textual, Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Microsoft Presidio, Haiku 4.5 and GLiNER2.
Some of the most valuable training data for frontier AI models lives inside fully functioning companies. It captures years of real work across decisions, communications, tools, handoffs, exceptions and the relationships connecting them.
The problem is that this data is also full of PII.
Traditional redaction makes the data safe, but it also destroys the very workflows and relationships frontier models need to learn from.
flow-transform 1.0 solves this by turning enterprise operational data into high-fidelity training data for frontier models by replacing real-world identities without flattening the reality the data captures.
item.content:encoded:
Today we’re launching micro1’s PII transformation model, flow-transform 1.0, delivering frontier-level performance across detection, identity synthesis, and transformation of personally identifiable information.

On PrivacyBench, our model reaches 96.0% F1, outperforming every detection baseline we tested, including Tonic Textual, Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Microsoft Presidio, Haiku 4.5 and GLiNER2.

Some of the most valuable training data for frontier AI models lives inside fully functioning companies. It captures years of real work across decisions, communications, tools, handoffs, exceptions and the relationships connecting them.

The problem is that this data is also full of PII.

Traditional redaction makes the data safe, but it also destroys the very workflows and relationships frontier models need to learn from.

flow-transform 1.0 solves this by turning enterprise operational data into high-fidelity training data for frontier models by replacing real-world identities without flattening the reality the data captures.

item.title: @wallstengine: ODYSSEY LAUNCHES AGORA-2 FOR MULTI-AGENT AI SIMULATION Agora-2 is a new world model that can simula...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ODYSSEY LAUNCHES AGORA-2 FOR MULTI-AGENT AI SIMULATION
Agora-2 is a new world model that can simulate up to 20 humans and AI agents interacting inside the same generated environment in real time, 5x more participants than Agora-1.
There’s no traditional game engine underneath. The world itself is generated by the model, and each participant’s actions affect the environment for everyone else.
The research preview supports up to 4 humans alongside 16 AI agents.
Odyssey sees the technology being used to train and test agents for robotics, autonomous vehicles, defense, cybersecurity and AI safety.

item.title: @wallstengine: Google will launch an experimental AI satellite on Oct. 1 as part of Project Suncatcher, its effort...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Google will launch an experimental AI satellite on Oct. 1 as part of Project Suncatcher, its effort to eventually build AI data centers in space.
The satellite will carry 4 $GOOGL TPUs and enough compute to answer simple Gemini queries from orbit while testing whether AI chips can reliably operate in space.
Google plans two more satellite launches in 2027 and is already designing potential fleets of 80+ satellites that could work together as an orbital AI data center.
Google estimates space-based data centers could become cost-competitive with terrestrial facilities by the mid-2030s.
Source: NYT

item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL, OPENAI, ANTHROPIC PLAN AI SAFETY BODY Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are moving ahead with pl...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL, OPENAI, ANTHROPIC PLAN AI SAFETY BODY
Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are moving ahead with plans to create an independent AI safety standards group, tentatively called the Standards Authority for Frontier AI, with a launch targeted for late 2026 or early 2027.
The group would:
• Set safety & security standards for frontier AI models • Support third-party testing before model releases • Create rules for reporting AI safety incidents • Set qualifications for independent model auditors • Potentially conduct its own model safety and capability testing
The effort is moving forward without government oversight after plans for a public-private framework stalled.
Source: The Information
item.content:encoded:
$GOOGL, OPENAI, ANTHROPIC PLAN AI SAFETY BODY

Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are moving ahead with plans to create an independent AI safety standards group, tentatively called the Standards Authority for Frontier AI, with a launch targeted for late 2026 or early 2027.

The group would:

• Set safety & security standards for frontier AI models
• Support third-party testing before model releases
• Create rules for reporting AI safety incidents
• Set qualifications for independent model auditors
• Potentially conduct its own model safety and capability testing

The effort is moving forward without government oversight after plans for a public-private framework stalled.

Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China is seeing a historic boom in exports due to AI. China’s exports rose +25% YoY in August, thei...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China is seeing a historic boom in exports due to AI.
China’s exports rose +25% YoY in August, their 3rd-largest monthly reading in at least 2 years.
At the same time, imports surged +28%, pushing the monthly trade surplus to +$119 billion and the year-to-date surplus to +$806 billion.
This puts China’s trade surplus on track for another annual record, following the $1.2 trillion seen in 2025.
This all comes as high-tech exports contributed more than half of China’s export growth last month.
Integrated-circuit shipments soared +130% YoY in August, while high-tech product exports jumped +57%.
The AI boom is increasingly powering China’s export engine.

This all comes as high-tech exports contributed more than half of China’s export growth last month.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +78.3% YoY in the first 20 days of September, its strongest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +78.3% YoY in the first 20 days of September, its strongest monthly growth on record.
This brought the value of exports to $71.4 billion, an all-time high.
This also marks the 5th consecutive month with growth of at least +50.0%.
Furthermore, exports adjusted for working-day differences rose +89.8% YoY, following a +61.5% increase during the same period in August.
Semiconductor exports were the key driver, surging +259.4% YoY to a record $34.1 billion.
Shipments to the US jumped +118.0% while shipments to China rose +113.8%,
South Korea has become an economic powerhouse.

item.title: @wallstengine: Micro1, founded by 25-year-old Ali Ansari, has raised $100M+ at a $4B valuation, according to Forbe...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Micro1, founded by 25-year-old Ali Ansari, has raised $100M+ at a $4B valuation, according to Forbes.
The company supplies training data to frontier AI labs and other AI companies.
At the start of 2025, it was a recruiting startup doing about $7M ARR. It has since pivoted into AI data and now reports $500M+ in annualized revenue.
Customers include Microsoft, Amazon, 1X and frontier labs, while two xAI cofounders and two frontier labs reportedly joined the new round.
Its valuation has jumped from $500M last September to $4B now.

item.title: @HedgeyeComm: We said in February that consumer agents would be the SaaS-mageddon equivalent for consumer interne...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeComm
item.description:
We said in February that consumer agents would be the SaaS-mageddon equivalent for consumer internet.
That 2H26 would be the second coming. Here we are.
SaaS-mageddon was a repricing of per-seat software. Once agents could run the workflow, the extra dashboard login stopped being worth a license.
Consumer internet runs on a different assumption… that a human still shows up, looks at the page, clicks the ad, compares options, and checks out themselves.
That layer is now under attack.
Muse is placing orders and calling support. Instinct is booking, researching, and running errands from iMessage. Amazon’s first move was to ban Muse from its site. That’s the tell.
The UI is no longer the product.
Bot traffic already crossed 50%. Action-taking agent traffic is up thousands of percent. Humans are becoming the rounding error on their own internet.
Marketplace take rates, ad impressions, time-on-site, branded apps, loyalty programs - all of that assumed the user would still do the work.
Once the agent is the customer, those surfaces either become APIs or they disappear.
February was the warning.
September is the start.

Consumer internet runs on a different assumption… that a human still shows up, looks at the page, clicks the ad, compares options, and checks out themselves.

That layer is now under attack.

Muse is placing orders and calling support. Instinct is booking, researching, and running errands from iMessage. Amazon’s first move was to ban Muse from its site. That’s the tell.

The UI is no longer the product.

Bot traffic already crossed 50%. Action-taking agent traffic is up thousands of percent. Humans are becoming the rounding error on their own internet.

Marketplace take rates, ad impressions, time-on-site, branded apps, loyalty programs - all of that assumed the user would still do the work.

Once the agent is the customer, those surfaces either become APIs or they disappear.

February was the warning.

September is the start.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Today marked the largest single-day gain in the 10Y Note Yield in 17 months, rising +15 basis point...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Today marked the largest single-day gain in the 10Y Note Yield in 17 months, rising +15 basis points.
The last time we saw a move of this magnitude? In April 2025, on “Liberation Day.”
This time, however, nothing notable happened today. This is just another day in the 2026 bond market.
Next, the market is pricing-in another 25 basis point Fed rate hike in October.
If the Fed is actually going to raise rates again in October, they should have hiked by 50 basis points on September 16th.
Keep in mind, just 9 months ago, markets thought the Fed would be on its third rate cut of 2026 by now.
It’s truly incredible how fast things can change in today’s markets.

item.title: @wallstengine: CLAUDE AUTONOMOUSLY DISCOVERED A NEW BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM Anthropic says Claude identified a previousl...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CLAUDE AUTONOMOUSLY DISCOVERED A NEW BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM
Anthropic says Claude identified a previously uncharacterized enzyme system in bacteriophage DNA with CRISPR-like repeat arrays, which it calls ART.
Around 950 Claude agents spent 21 hours and 210M tokens analyzing 200,000+ reverse transcriptases, finding 3,500 candidate systems and narrowing them to 20 before flagging ART for human review.
Anthropic scientists then validated the system in its new molecular biology lab.
Its function is still unknown, but Anthropic says the few known systems with similar features are programmable and can perform operations like cutting, copying and pasting DNA.
The company says this is the first result from its new life sciences lab, where Claude generates biological hypotheses and human scientists test the most promising ones experimentally. https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2102824961538920822/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: $SPCX STRIKES CLASSIFIED SPACE-TRACKING DEAL SpaceX has struck a deal with the U.S. Space Force giv...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$SPCX STRIKES CLASSIFIED SPACE-TRACKING DEAL
SpaceX has struck a deal with the U.S. Space Force giving it unique access to the Pentagon’s most detailed classified space-tracking data, according to Breaking Defense.
In return, SpaceX is sharing data from Stargaze, which uses ~30,000 cameras across Starlink satellites to track objects in low Earth orbit.
The classified data could help SpaceX more precisely model collision risks around its ~11,000 Starlink and Starshield satellites. SpaceX says its fleet performs ~20,000 maneuvers a day, including ~1,000 for collision avoidance.
The agreement restricts the Pentagon data to internal use and says it cannot be used for commercial gain.

The Trump administration is preparing a 90-day ban on US diesel exports as fuel prices continue to surge, with diesel averaging around $6.52 a gallon nationwide.
The goal would be to keep more diesel in the US and bring prices down in the short term.
Some officials and oil companies are pushing back on the idea. They say a ban could leave refiners with more diesel than they can sell, forcing them to cut production and potentially driving fuel prices higher.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright has publicly rejected the idea of a full export ban, saying it could send prices higher.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US M2 money supply jumped +$124.9 billion in August, to a record $23.34 trillion. This ma...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US M2 money supply jumped +$124.9 billion in August, to a record $23.34 trillion.
This marks the 28th consecutive monthly increase, totaling +$2.61 trillion.
YoY, M2 grew +5.7%, its largest YoY increase since June 2022.
This marks a sharp acceleration from +2.0% YoY growth seen in August 2024.
Meanwhile, since the 2020 pandemic, M2 money supply has surged +$7.85 trillion, equivalent to +$1.21 trillion on average per year, or +6.5% annualized growth.
US money creation is picking up speed.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on @ezraklein’s podcast says AI labs don’t need outside help to slow down:...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on @ezraklein’s podcast says AI labs don’t need outside help to slow down:
“If I believe that I’m about to launch a product that is unsafe, it is completely in my ability, my power and my responsibility to not launch the product.”
"The fact of the matter is, there are so many laws, there's so many obligations, they're so incentivized to ship safe products."
"If they ship unsafe products, their customers go away. If they ship unsafe products and they harm somebody, they could have a civil lawsuit."
"If they ship some something, and they did it knowingly, there could be negligence involved. There could be criminal lawsuits."
"The fact of the matter is, there are plenty of incentives for them to do it right. So I just, I have to disagree with your premise about somehow somebody's pushing them to do this."
Source: The New York Times / The Ezra Klein Show

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China’s exports to the US are rebounding sharply: Chinese exports to the US surged +34% YoY in Augu...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China’s exports to the US are rebounding sharply:
Chinese exports to the US surged +34% YoY in August to $42.5 billion, surpassing $40.0 billion for the 3rd consecutive month.
This marks the 5th consecutive month of growth and the 2nd-largest YoY increase in at least 5 years.
Growth has also doubled from July’s +17% YoY increase.
By comparison, in August 2025, China’s exports to the US dropped -33% YoY, to $31.6 billion.
The recent surge was driven by stronger demand for AI-related electronics produced in China, which is supporting stronger shipments despite ongoing trade tensions.
Chinese exports are making a powerful comeback despite tariffs.

item.title: @WatcherGuru: JUST IN: Morgan Stanley accidentally leaks internal document containing details of more than 100 in...
item.dc:creator: @WatcherGuru
item.description:
JUST IN: Morgan Stanley accidentally leaks internal document containing details of more than 100 investment banking deals.
A Morgan Stanley employee mistakenly emailed an internal document revealing details on more than 100 investment-banking deals, primarily across Asia.
The document included potential IPOs from China, South Korea and India, along with information on private-equity and pension-fund backers and projects that had been paused.
The employee later attempted to retract the email, while a blurred copy surfaced on Instagram.
Morgan Stanley said it acted quickly to address the leak and is working with the parties involved.

item.title: @HedgeyeComm: FIVE DIMENSIONS OF AGENT-ERA ADVANTAGE Conventional frameworks for platform dominance -software, in...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeComm
item.description:
FIVE DIMENSIONS OF AGENT-ERA ADVANTAGE
Conventional frameworks for platform dominance -software, infrastructure, data - explain the current landscape but fail to predict where value accrues in the agent era. They overweight infrastructure ownership, which is commoditizing, and underweight the user relationship, which is becoming the scarcest asset in the stack.
We use five dimensions instead. Each compounds over time, and strength across several creates a flywheel that becomes very hard to replicate.
1️⃣ Contextual Depth How well does the platform know the user?
There are two ways to acquire it:
Observational context comes from passively watching behavior - social graph, purchase history, location, content preferences. Meta is the undisputed leader, with the most comprehensive behavioral graph on humans ever assembled.
Collaborative context comes from direct, active interaction - instructions, corrections, workflow patterns, work product, conversation history. This is what accumulates when you use Claude daily.
The distinction matters enormously... $META knows what you like. Claude learns how you work. Both are valuable, but collaborative context compounds with usage in a way observational context does not. Every correction deepens the relationship and raises the switching cost.
2️⃣ Workflow Entrenchment How deeply is the agent embedded in daily operations?
Every MCP connector configured, every agent built, every automated workflow deployed is an investment that creates lock-in... not contractual lock-in, the traditional SaaS model, but behavioral lock-in. Users don't switch because their operating rhythm is built around the agent.
This is where Anthropic is building the deepest moat... Claude Code, Projects, computer use, MCP. The critical insight is that workflow entrenchment can be built without owning infrastructure. It is earned through utility, not capital expenditure.
3️⃣ Ecosystem Density How many connectors, integrations and third-party developers are building for the platform?
Classic network effects applied to the agent layer. Every new connector makes the agent more useful, which drives more users, which attracts more developers. $GOOGL is building this through the Universal Commerce Protocol and GCP. Anthropic is building it through MCP and the developer community - and none of it requires a data center.
And now $META is trying to build it with connectors and @Muse...
4️⃣ Intelligence Edge Model quality in the domains that matter - not benchmarks, but real workflows. Anthropic's sustained edge in coding and enterprise reasoning is why developers chose Claude and kept choosing it. Google's native multimodality is why Apple partnered with them. Intelligence edge can shift as models leapfrog, but combined with Workflow Entrenchment - users build workflows around a model's specific strengths - it is stickier than capability scores suggest.
The biggest open question for the entire thesis: does intelligence edge remain a durable moat, or do base models converge faster than ecosystems compound?
If models fully commoditize, the first three dimensions become the only sustainable advantages - and that favors whoever gets to scale first.
5️⃣ Distribution Surface How does the platform reach users at scale?
Apple has 2B+ devices. Google has default search on nearly every browser plus Android. Meta has 3B+ users but not the OS underneath.
In the agent era, distribution has a recursive property... strong performance on the first four dimensions generates distribution rather than requiring it as a precondition. If Claude is your daily interface and Claude connects to everything, Claude is your distribution surface for every downstream application. That's fundamentally different from the mobile era, where you needed the App Store to reach users.
THE FLYWHEEL More usage deepens Contextual Depth → drives Workflow Entrenchment → attracts developers and builds Ecosystem Density → reinforces Intelligence Edge through real-world usage data → expands Distribution Surface → feeds back into more usage. It can operate without infrastructure ownership at any step.
Infrastructure ownership isn't a prerequisite for competing. But it is a margin multiplier for those who have it - which brings us to the most important structural dynamic in the landscape....

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: After a brief intermission, back to the regularly scheduled programming. The 10Y Note Yield is back...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
After a brief intermission, back to the regularly scheduled programming.
The 10Y Note Yield is back to its highest levels since 2023 and the 30Y Note Yield is up to 5.35%, matching 2007 levels.
Despite numerous intervention attempts by the US Treasury, nothing is working.
It is becoming increasingly clear that the only way to drive yields lower over the short-run would be an end to the Iran War and the ongoing global energy crisis.
However, over the long-run, this is a structural problem, with deficit spending and years of compounding inflation at its core.
The reality is that the era of ultra-low rates that Americans and the world became used to will not return anytime soon.
"Higher for longer" is the new normal.
item.content:encoded:

It is becoming increasingly clear that the only way to drive yields lower over the short-run would be an end to the Iran War and the ongoing global energy crisis.

However, over the long-run, this is a structural problem, with deficit spending and years of compounding inflation at its core.

The reality is that the era of ultra-low rates that Americans and the world became used to will not return anytime soon.

"Higher for longer" is the new normal.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: US corporate net interest payments are down to just 0.4% of GDP, their lo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
US corporate net interest payments are down to just 0.4% of GDP, their lowest in at least 10 years.
This percentage has declined -1.2 points since 2022, despite the Fed hiking rates from 0.25% to 5.50% between 2022 and 2023.
This comes as many companies locked in ultra-low fixed rates during the pandemic, protecting their interest costs from the subsequent rise in rates.
Over the same period, US government net interest costs have increased +1.2 percentage points to 3.6% of GDP, near their highest in at least 10 years.
Unlike corporates, the US government did not lock in enough ultra-low rates in 2020, leaving it increasingly exposed to much higher interest costs as rates rose.
The US government is taking the biggest hit from higher rates.

item.title: @Hedgeye: "Impact scales through aggregation. Structure emerges from repetition." -Rich Brennan Brennan says...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
"Impact scales through aggregation. Structure emerges from repetition." -Rich Brennan
Brennan says this is how a market actually builds itself, starting with a single trade.
On its own, one trade barely matters. Most get absorbed and cancel each other out.
But when thousands of small trades start leaning the same way, buying attracts more buying. That's how a trend forms.
Zoom in and it looks like noise. Zoom out and there's a structure that was there all along.
Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough says AI is now one of the biggest participants in the market. Its trades feed back like everyone else's. They aggregate, they repeat, and over time they build structure.
Same with the dots below. Each one lands at random, and after 60,000 of them a triangle appears.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Global government debt has surged to unprecedented levels: The Debt-to-GDP ratio of emerging market...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Global government debt has surged to unprecedented levels:
The Debt-to-GDP ratio of emerging market economies is up to ~78%, its highest level in data going back to 1880.
Since the 2008 Financial Crisis, this metric has more than doubled and surpassed the ~45% peak seen during World War II.
Before 2020, this ratio never exceeded 60% and is now approaching 80% for the first time.
Meanwhile, the Debt-to-GDP ratio of advanced economies is up to ~108% and has been above 100% for the last 10 years.
Before the 2008 Financial Crisis, this figure stood below 80%.
Deficit spending has become a global crisis.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MSFT PLANS DEEPER COPILOT DISCOUNTS ALONGSIDE NEW AI “SUPER APP”
Microsoft is preparing discounts of 30%-50% on corporate Copilot subscriptions as it looks to drive broader enterprise adoption, per The Information.
The discounts are expected to start in October, with roughly 30% off for customers buying 1,000+ seats and up to 50% for those buying 10,000+ seats. Copilot currently starts at $30 per user per month.
At the same time, Microsoft plans to launch a revamped Copilot “super app” as soon as this week, combining AI coding tools and OpenClaw-style agent capabilities in one app.
Some of those new features will carry usage-based charges, allowing Microsoft to discount the base subscription while generating additional revenue as customers use more AI features.
Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Americans are increasingly worried about their jobs. The perceived probability among US consumers t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Americans are increasingly worried about their jobs.
The perceived probability among US consumers that the unemployment rate will be higher in 1-year increased +1.6 percentage points in August, to 44.4%, its highest since April 2020.
Excluding the 2020 pandemic, this marks the highest reading since the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations began in 2013.
By comparison, this indicator peaked at 44.1% in April 2025, following uncertainty around tariffs.
By income, the perceived probability of a rise in unemployment was the highest among those earning over $100,000, at 50.3%, the 2nd-highest reading on record.
By comparison, expectations stood at 43.5% among those earning $50,000-$100,000, the 2nd-highest reading since March 2025, and 38.0% among those earning under $50,000, the highest since May.
Fear of unemployment is rising.

item.title: @wallstengine: CFTC DELAYS CME’S PLAN FOR $NVDA GPU RENTAL FUTURES CME Group’s planned futures contracts tied to N...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CFTC DELAYS CME’S PLAN FOR $NVDA GPU RENTAL FUTURES
CME Group’s planned futures contracts tied to Nvidia H100 and B200 rental prices won’t launch in October as originally targeted, per The Information.
The CFTC extended its review by 45 days, through Nov. 9, citing “novel or complex” issues and concerns around potential market manipulation.
The contracts would let AI companies, compute providers and lenders hedge swings in GPU rental prices, effectively creating a financial market around AI compute.
The challenge is that GPU rental prices are still fragmented and largely set through private contracts, making reliable pricing benchmarks harder to establish.
Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US equity mutual funds are significantly underweight AI equities: Large-cap mutual funds are now ~1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US equity mutual funds are significantly underweight AI equities:
Large-cap mutual funds are now ~1.75 percentage points underweight AI-exposed stocks versus their benchmarks, the largest underweight position on record.
This excludes mega-cap names such as Amazon, $AMZN, Broadcom, $AVGO, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Nvidia, $NVDA.
By comparison, in mid-2024, they were overweight AI-related names versus their benchmarks by 0.40 percentage points.
This comes as AI-exposed equities now make up 13.0% of the average large-cap mutual fund portfolio, versus 14.8% in their respective benchmarks.
By comparison, both metrics stood at ~6.5% in Q3 2024.
Institutional portfolios are underexposed to the AI trade.

item.title: @wallstengine: $QCOM UNVEILS NEW 2NM SNAPDRAGON CHIPS WITH BIG ON-DEVICE AI PUSH Qualcomm launched the Snapdragon...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$QCOM UNVEILS NEW 2NM SNAPDRAGON CHIPS WITH BIG ON-DEVICE AI PUSH
Qualcomm launched the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and higher-end Extreme Gen 6, its first 2nm smartphone chips.
The biggest focus is local AI. The chips include a sensing hub that can run models up to 200M parameters for things like speaker recognition, personal memory and always-on assistants.
The Extreme version can run up to a 30B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model locally on the phone.
It also supports 8K/60fps and 4K/240fps video, while both chips add AI-based voice isolation and noise reduction.
Motorola, Xiaomi, Vivo, Oppo, Honor, OnePlus and others are expected to use the new chips.

item.title: @wallstengine: $IONQ DEMONSTRATES REAL-TIME QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION ON A SINGLE CPU IonQ says it demonstrated wha...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$IONQ DEMONSTRATES REAL-TIME QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION ON A SINGLE CPU
IonQ says it demonstrated what it calls the industry’s first end-to-end real-time quantum error correction decoder running on a standard off-the-shelf CPU.
The system was tested on benchmark circuits simulating up to 408 logical qubits and more than 31.5M quantum operations, with as little as 0.02% added processing time.
The decoder runs continuously in the background, allowing error correction without pausing quantum execution.
IonQ says the result supports its Walking Cat architecture and roadmap toward systems controlling thousands of qubits.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China imported +1,141 tonnes of gold in the first 8 months of 2026, its largest import on record for this period of the year.
This figure already exceeds China’s gold imports for the full year 2025.
At this pace, China’s annual gold imports will surpass 1,700 tonnes for the first time.
Furthermore, China’s ETFs added +44 tonnes of gold in the first 8 months of the year, up +18% YoY.
The surge has been driven by strong investment demand, economic uncertainty, and a strong yuan that created favorable conditions for gold imports from abroad.
China is stockpiling gold like never before.

Royal Caribbean is nearing a deal to buy a majority stake in Sandals Resorts International, valuing the company at more than $6 billion.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Semiconductor ETFs are making history. Assets under management (AUM) in the semiconductor ETF, $SMH...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Semiconductor ETFs are making history.
Assets under management (AUM) in the semiconductor ETF, $SMH, are up to $70 billion, near its highest level since July.
At the same time, AUM in the semiconductor ETF, $SOXX, are up to $46 billion, near its highest on record.
This comes as $SMH's AUM has grown more than +500% since the start of 2024, while $SOXX's AUM has grown +360%.
By comparison, AUM in the tech software ETF, $IGV, has risen +91% over the same period, to $13.5 billion.
As a result, the two semiconductor ETFs now hold ~$116 billion in assets combined.
The semiconductor trade is incredibly hot.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: The Yield Curve Is The Biggest Problem Since 2022
🔊
On Tuesday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough explained why the falling yield curve is the biggest macro problem since 2022 and why it is a reason to stay away from the financials.
"It is probably the biggest problem we've seen since the beginning of 2022," the year Hedgeye called the crash after 2021's Quad 2 top.
The sequence is the same, first Quad 2, then Quad 4, and the curve is now diving toward 19 basis points.
It draws attention only once it turns negative, and by then the damage is done.
On the way there, while stocks push higher, almost no one flags it.
"Do not buy the financials on that," McCullough says.

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 performs at roughly the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most tasks, while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5 and generating output 30%+ faster.
Here’s everything you need to know:
Opus 5.5 is Anthropic’s new flagship model, with major gains in agentic coding, computer use and knowledge work.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are coming in the next few weeks.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +27.1 tonnes in inflows last week, the 3rd lar...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +27.1 tonnes in inflows last week, the 3rd largest weekly inflow since January.
Demand was driven by the US, at +15.9 tonnes, followed by Europe and Asia, at +6.5 tonnes and +4.6 tonnes, respectively.
In Dollar terms, investors bought +$3.9 billion, the 4th-largest weekly inflow since February.
This also marks the 11th consecutive weekly inflow.
Over this period, global gold ETFs have attracted +208.3 tonnes in inflows, bringing total gold ETF holdings to a record 4,250 tonnes.
Demand for gold ETFs remains remarkably strong.

item.title: @wallstengine: MORE DETAILS ON DIGITALOCEAN’S NEW MANAGED AGENTS: Each agent session runs inside its own isolated...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MORE DETAILS ON DIGITALOCEAN’S NEW MANAGED AGENTS:
Each agent session runs inside its own isolated Firecracker microVM, with its files, processes and context preserved even when the session is paused.
DigitalOcean only charges for CPU actually being used.
A 2-vCPU agent averaging 25% utilization for an hour will cost about $0.06 in CPU + memory vs. $0.126 if the full allocated capacity were billed.
Paused sessions stop CPU and memory charges while keeping their state, and DigitalOcean says they can resume in about 305ms.
The Action Gateway gives agents access to 16,000+ tools across 500+ providers, while keeping credentials outside both the model and the sandbox. Sensitive actions can also be set to require human approval.
DigitalOcean says its tool discovery system matched agent intent to the correct tool with 99.3% accuracy in internal testing.
Early customer Qencode says its support agent is already saving roughly 4-8 hours per week and reducing some response times from hours to nearly instant.
I’d definitely use the $0.06 vs $0.126 example + 305ms resume + credentials never reaching the agent. Those three make the product much easier to understand than another generic “one cloud, one bill” post.

DigitalOcean says its tool discovery system matched agent intent to the correct tool with 99.3% accuracy in internal testing.

Early customer Qencode says its support agent is already saving roughly 4-8 hours per week and reducing some response times from hours to nearly instant.

I’d definitely use the $0.06 vs $0.126 example + 305ms resume + credentials never reaching the agent. Those three make the product much easier to understand than another generic “one cloud, one bill” post.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Institutional investors are cutting their bullish bets on the US Dollar. Long speculative positioni...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Institutional investors are cutting their bullish bets on the US Dollar.
Long speculative positioning in the US Dollar fell -$15 billion, to +$5 billion in the week ending September 15th, the lowest since March.
This covers hedge funds, speculative currency traders, and asset managers.
This marks the 7th consecutive weekly decline, the longest streak since Q1 2025.
By comparison, bullish bets on the US Dollar peaked at ~$50 billion in mid-July.
Meanwhile, the US Dollar Index rose +1.4% last week, its biggest weekly gain since May 2026, following the Fed’s first rate hike since July 2023.
The US Dollar is seeing extreme volatility.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The number of weekly spot DEX trades on Solana has officially surpassed the NYSE for the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The number of weekly spot DEX trades on Solana has officially surpassed the NYSE for the first time in history.
This metric includes the number of individual onchain token swaps executed on decentralized exchanges built on Solana.
In the week ending September 13th, Solana saw ~208 million spot DEX trades, compared to ~190 million on the NYSE.
Meanwhile, the gap between the Nasdaq and Solana narrowed to ~47 million trades, the smallest gap on record.
The growth has been largely catalyzed by Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, which has processed over 80 million trades this month, up +38% month-over-month.
To put this into perspective, Solana has now seen +185% growth in weekly spot DEX trade volumes compared to the lows seen in July.
Crypto markets are on fire.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AMGN PHASE 3 SJÖGREN’S TRIAL HITS PRIMARY ENDPOINT Amgen says dazodalibep significantly improved s...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AMGN PHASE 3 SJÖGREN’S TRIAL HITS PRIMARY ENDPOINT
Amgen says dazodalibep significantly improved systemic disease activity in patients with moderate-to-severe Sjögren’s disease, with benefits seen as early as Week 4 and sustained through Week 48.
The Phase 3 OASIZ 301 trial enrolled about 621 patients and met its primary endpoint based on the ESSDAI disease activity score.
There are currently no FDA-approved medicines for Sjögren’s disease.
A second Phase 3 study, OASIZ 303, focused on symptomatic Sjögren’s, is expected to complete in Q4.

$ITRI PARTNERS WITH CRYTICA TO EMBED CYBER THREAT DETECTION DIRECTLY INTO GRID-EDGE DEVICES
Itron is integrating Crytica Security’s RDAi technology into its Grid Edge Intelligence platform to continuously monitor utility meters, meter-hosted apps and other edge workloads.
Crytica’s probe is under 100KB and can detect unauthorized changes to device instructions within seconds, allowing it to run on resource-constrained grid equipment where traditional endpoint security tools may not work.
The system is designed to cover both IT and operational technology environments, while also generating alerts around device health and reliability.

In other words, US earnings growth has been 2.6 times larger than the rest of the world.
This comes as global ex-US profit growth has remained roughly unchanged between 2008 and 2025.
The US economy is in a league of its own.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China’s loan growth is collapsing: China’s loans grew +4.9% YoY in August, its weakest reading in d...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China’s loan growth is collapsing:
China’s loans grew +4.9% YoY in August, its weakest reading in data going back to the 1990s.
This comes as bank lending fell to just ~$9 billion, materially below the ~$60 billion expected.
Furthermore, aggregate financing, a broad measure of credit, increased just +$247 billion, well below the +$314 billion expected.
Loan growth has trended lower for years and peaked at 34.2% YoY, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Weak borrowing from households and businesses is driving the slowdown, with household mid- and long-term loans shrinking for the 5th month this year.
At the same time, comparable corporate loans fell to more than 50% below their 2023 levels.
China’s economy is struggling.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US household equity exposure now accounts for a record 39.9% of household net worth. This...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US household equity exposure now accounts for a record 39.9% of household net worth.
This figure has surged +12.6 percentage points since the 2022 bear market.
Over the same period, owners’ equity in residential real estate as a % of household net worth has declined -3.5 percentage points, to 19.3%, its lowest proportion since Q2 2021.
This metric measures the market value of homes minus outstanding mortgage and home loan debt held by households, as a % of total household net worth.
As a result, the gap between equity exposure and real estate exposure has risen to a record 20.6 percentage points.
To put this into perspective, real estate exposure peaked at 24.1% in Q3 2005, during the housing boom, and was 1.0 percentage point above equity exposure.
Household wealth has never been this skewed toward equities.

$LLY BREAKS GROUND ON $6.5B HOUSTON PLANT TO MAKE ORAL GLP-1 DRUG FOUNDaYO
Eli Lilly has started construction on a roughly 1M-square-foot manufacturing site in Houston, its 10th U.S. manufacturing site announced since 2020.
The facility will produce active pharmaceutical ingredients for Foundayo, Lilly’s FDA-approved oral GLP-1 weight-loss pill, along with other small-molecule and advanced medicines.
Lilly expects the site to create 615 permanent jobs and about 4,000 construction jobs, with build-out taking roughly five years.
The plant is part of Lilly’s broader $50B U.S. manufacturing investment program.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI goods are driving historic global trade growth: Global trade in AI-enabling goods surged +42% Yo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI goods are driving historic global trade growth:
Global trade in AI-enabling goods surged +42% YoY in Q1 2026, the largest annual growth rate on record.
This is up from +22% growth for the full year 2025 and +11% in 2024.
At the same time, trade in non-AI goods grew only +7% YoY, up from +5% in 2025 and +1% in 2024.
This pushed total global goods trade growth to +12% YoY in Q1 2026, up from +7% in 2025 and just +2% in 2024.
As a result, AI-enabling goods accounted for 18.7% of world trade in Q1, up from 13.8% in 2024.
AI is the new engine of global trade growth.

$VICR RAISES Q3 REVENUE GROWTH OUTLOOK TO 20%+ ON POWER DELIVERY ROYALTIES
Vicor now expects Q3 revenue to grow more than 20% sequentially, up from its prior outlook of nearly 10%, driven by royalties from a new non-exclusive license for its Vertical Power Delivery technology.
Vicor says four leading OEMs and hyperscalers have now licensed its power-system technology.
CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli said some hyperscalers approached Vicor after computing systems using infringing power modules were blocked from import, and as they recognized systems using unlicensed VPD technology could face similar action.
Vicor says the licensing model gives OEMs access to multiple suppliers while generating royalty revenue from its patented power-delivery architecture.

item.title: @wallstengine: TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES $5B MIDDLE EAST ENERGY REBUILD FUND: WSJ The U.S. is proposing $5B fo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES $5B MIDDLE EAST ENERGY REBUILD FUND: WSJ
The U.S. is proposing $5B for a new fund to rebuild energy infrastructure damaged in the Iran war and reduce regional dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.
Washington would seek matching contributions from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq and Jordan, potentially bringing the fund to $10B.
The fund, called Pact, would be managed by the U.S. Development Finance Corporation. Discussions are still ongoing and terms could change.
The proposal comes as Hormuz traffic remains sharply below pre-war levels and Gulf producers continue using costly workarounds to move oil.
item.content:encoded:
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES $5B MIDDLE EAST ENERGY REBUILD FUND: WSJ

The U.S. is proposing $5B for a new fund to rebuild energy infrastructure damaged in the Iran war and reduce regional dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.

Washington would seek matching contributions from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq and Jordan, potentially bringing the fund to $10B.

The fund, called Pact, would be managed by the U.S. Development Finance Corporation. Discussions are still ongoing and terms could change.

The proposal comes as Hormuz traffic remains sharply below pre-war levels and Gulf producers continue using costly workarounds to move oil.

item.title: @wallstengine: SOFTBANK-BACKED SB ENERGY DELAYS IPO AS INVESTORS PUSH BACK ON $50B+ VALUATION SB Energy has pushed...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SOFTBANK-BACKED SB ENERGY DELAYS IPO AS INVESTORS PUSH BACK ON $50B+ VALUATION
SB Energy has pushed its IPO from September to at least mid-to-late October after struggling to find enough buyers at its targeted $50B+ valuation, per NYT.
A major concern is execution risk: SB Energy has yet to put a data center into operation, while projecting a $439B revenue backlog over roughly 20 years beginning in 2028, largely tied to its massive Ohio data center leased to OpenAI and backed by Nvidia.
Last week, SB Energy brought OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar and infrastructure chief Sachin Katti onto an investor call as it tried to address investor concerns.
The delay comes as appetite for data-center IPOs cools, with Holtec pausing its offering and Aggreko also slowing its process.
Source: NYT

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China is rapidly accelerating its AI buildout. As a result, the US and China's AI arms race appears...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China is rapidly accelerating its AI buildout.
As a result, the US and China's AI arms race appears to be at its most intense point yet.
Worldwide data center CapEx is now expected to surpass $3 trillion by 2030, and that outlook has nearly doubled since January 2026 alone.
This growth in CapEx expectations is being driven by hyperscale spending, power capacity needs, and rising construction costs.
In fact, the top 20 tech companies in the US are now spending 16% of revenue on CapEx, compared to 9% in China.
As a result, the US is maintaining its lead on frontier AI models while China is pushing ahead on cost-optimized models and accelerating adoption.
The US and China are in the midst of a historic technological competition.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CODOS LAUNCHES “VIRTUAL CHIEF AI OFFICER” FOR ENTERPRISE AI TRANSFORMATION
Codos launched a platform designed to automate much of the work companies typically rely on consultants and internal AI teams to do.
The system interviews employees across an organization, identifies where work can be automated, deploys a company-wide AI knowledge layer called EnterpriseRAG, and then helps run the transformation across functions like sales, engineering, operations and customer support.
It can also run on a company’s own servers.
Codos says it is already working with Nasdaq-listed and PE-backed companies and has generated more than $10M in impact for customers.
In one midsize fintech deployment, the company says a six-month rollout unlocked 21% of total FTE capacity through automations including agentic onboarding, QA, finance and customer-support agents.
The broader bet is that AI transformation itself can become a software product rather than a consulting engagement.
https://x.com/dimakhanarin/status/2102065316406997475/video/1

OPENAI HAS LARGELY AUTOMATED TRAINING OF NEW EXPERIMENTAL AI MODELS
OpenAI’s internal AI models can now handle much of the process of building and training experimental models, including writing GPU kernels and optimizing the code used to run them.
Researchers can reportedly give an AI a single example of the optimization they want, then let it work for weeks implementing and testing similar improvements.
OpenAI employees also say internal agents increasingly collaborate with each other to solve problems without involving their human users.
The capability has improved significantly in just the last few months, while OpenAI’s growing access to compute is allowing researchers to test ideas much faster. Employees said some experiments that previously could have taken years can now be carried out in about a week.
Source: The Information

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI & ANTHROPIC NEARED LEGALLY BINDING DEAL TO STRESS-TEST EACH OTHER’S AI MODELS OpenAI and Ant...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI & ANTHROPIC NEARED LEGALLY BINDING DEAL TO STRESS-TEST EACH OTHER’S AI MODELS
OpenAI and Anthropic were close earlier this year to an agreement that would let each company test the other’s AI models for vulnerabilities and hidden safety risks, The Information reports.
The proposed arrangement would:
Give each lab API access to the other’s commercially available models. Allow them to independently run safety and vulnerability tests
Prevent either company from retaining the other’s testing data. This does not include access to unreleased models
It’s unclear whether the agreement was ultimately finalized.
The companies already ran a similar mutual evaluation in 2025. OpenAI found Anthropic models more likely to conceal rule-breaking behavior, while Anthropic found OpenAI models more willing to assist with potentially harmful requests.
The renewed talks came before a series of incidents involving OpenAI’s unreleased AI agents, including systems that reportedly accessed external and internal systems in unexpected ways.
Since then, OpenAI has:
• Paused a form of reinforcement-learning training for two weeks while improving monitoring • Temporarily reassigned 25% of its production engineering team to security work • Built monitoring systems that can require compute equal to roughly 20% of the inference workload being monitored
OpenAI has also reportedly largely automated the training process for new experimental models, with AI increasingly able to modify experiments, run them and monitor results with limited human intervention.
Source: The Information
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI & ANTHROPIC NEARED LEGALLY BINDING DEAL TO STRESS-TEST EACH OTHER’S AI MODELS

OpenAI and Anthropic were close earlier this year to an agreement that would let each company test the other’s AI models for vulnerabilities and hidden safety risks, The Information reports.

The proposed arrangement would:

Give each lab API access to the other’s commercially available models. Allow them to independently run safety and vulnerability tests

Prevent either company from retaining the other’s testing data. This does not include access to unreleased models

It’s unclear whether the agreement was ultimately finalized.

The companies already ran a similar mutual evaluation in 2025. OpenAI found Anthropic models more likely to conceal rule-breaking behavior, while Anthropic found OpenAI models more willing to assist with potentially harmful requests.

The renewed talks came before a series of incidents involving OpenAI’s unreleased AI agents, including systems that reportedly accessed external and internal systems in unexpected ways.

Since then, OpenAI has:

• Paused a form of reinforcement-learning training for two weeks while improving monitoring
• Temporarily reassigned 25% of its production engineering team to security work
• Built monitoring systems that can require compute equal to roughly 20% of the inference workload being monitored

OpenAI has also reportedly largely automated the training process for new experimental models, with AI increasingly able to modify experiments, run them and monitor results with limited human intervention.

Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Last week marked hedge funds' largest weekly purchase of US equities in 5 weeks. This was...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Last week marked hedge funds' largest weekly purchase of US equities in 5 weeks.
This was driven by short covering in macro products, such as index futures and ETFs, as well as long purchases of single stocks.
The strongest demand was seen in Information Technology and Communication Services.
Hedge funds have now purchased equities in these sectors for 3 consecutive weeks.
Furthermore, hedge funds have bought US software stocks for 4 consecutive weeks and in 6 of the last 8.
As a result, hedge fund allocation to software rose to ~5.0% of their total market exposure, its highest level since the start of the year, up from a record low of 1.3% set in February.
Hedge funds are adding more tech exposure.

item.description:
$COIN LAUNCHES IPO ACCESS FOR U.S. RETAIL INVESTORS, STARTING WITH OURA
Coinbase will now let eligible U.S. customers request IPO shares at the offer price before public trading begins.
The first deal available will be Oura’s upcoming IPO.
Users can submit a requested share amount through Coinbase, though allocations are not guaranteed and may be filled fully, partially or not at all depending on demand.
Coinbase is also adding an anti-flipping rule: investors who sell IPO shares within 30 days may be blocked from participating in future IPOs for 60 days, while repeated early selling could reduce future allocations.
The service is offered through Coinbase Capital Markets, its FINRA-registered broker-dealer.

item.title: @wallstengine: MORE DETAILS ON $META’S NEW PETAL SUBSEA CABLE: Instead of simply packing more fibers into the cabl...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MORE DETAILS ON $META’S NEW PETAL SUBSEA CABLE:
Instead of simply packing more fibers into the cable, Meta is using 2-core fiber, meaning two separate light paths run through a single strand roughly the width of a human hair.
Petal will use 24 fiber pairs with two cores each, effectively giving it the capacity of a conventional 48-pair system.
That allows Petal to reach 1 petabit per second, or about 125 terabytes of data every second. At full capacity, that’s roughly 1 petabyte every 8 seconds.
For perspective, Meta says that’s enough capacity for roughly 6.25 billion people, about 75% of the world’s population, to stream music at the same time.
Petal will also carry about 5.5x the capacity of Marea, Meta’s first transatlantic cable investment, without a proportional increase in power or physical infrastructure.
Meta says the design could help move multi-core fiber from experimental technology into mainstream subsea infrastructure.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META UNVEILS FIRST PETABIT-SCALE TRANSATLANTIC CABLE BETWEEN U.S. AND FRANCE Meta announced Petal,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META UNVEILS FIRST PETABIT-SCALE TRANSATLANTIC CABLE BETWEEN U.S. AND FRANCE
Meta announced Petal, a new roughly 7,000-km subsea cable designed to carry 1 petabit per second between the U.S. and France when it enters service in 2029.
Meta says that is roughly 2x the capacity of today’s most advanced transoceanic cables and represents the largest single-generation capacity jump for a transoceanic system.
Petal will use multi-core fiber technology across transoceanic distances, allowing more data to move through each fiber without a proportional increase in power or physical infrastructure.
The system is being developed with NEC and Sumitomo Electric, while Orange will support the French landing.

item.content:encoded:
$META UNVEILS FIRST PETABIT-SCALE TRANSATLANTIC CABLE BETWEEN U.S. AND FRANCE

Meta announced Petal, a new roughly 7,000-km subsea cable designed to carry 1 petabit per second between the U.S. and France when it enters service in 2029.

Meta says that is roughly 2x the capacity of today’s most advanced transoceanic cables and represents the largest single-generation capacity jump for a transoceanic system.

Petal will use multi-core fiber technology across transoceanic distances, allowing more data to move through each fiber without a proportional increase in power or physical infrastructure.

The system is being developed with NEC and Sumitomo Electric, while Orange will support the French landing.

The project adds to Meta’s growing global network infrastructure as AI workloads drive sharply higher bandwidth requirements between data centers and regions.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
FORMER ANTHROPIC RESEARCHER JACOB COXON BRIEFS 100+ TOP NYC BUSINESS LEADERS ON AI RISKS
Jacob Coxon recently spoke virtually with more than 100 members of the Partnership for New York City, in what one attendee described as one of the group’s most highly attended meetings in recent memory.
The Partnership represents 300+ companies, with board members including BlackRock CEO Larry Fink, JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, IBM CEO Arvind Krishna and NYSE Group President Lynn Martin.
The session was largely Q&A, with executives questioning Coxon on AI-driven cybersecurity risks, regulation, effective altruism and whether AI ultimately requires a global regulatory framework.
The group typically hosts major executives and policymakers focused on issues directly affecting New York businesses, making Coxon’s appearance unusual.
One attendee compared the level of interest to Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla’s updates to the group during the pandemic.
Source: NYT DealBook

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
EINRIDE TO BUILD NEXT-GEN AUTONOMOUS TRUCKING STACK ON $NVDA HYPERION
Swedish freight company Einride $ENRD is partnering with Nvidia to adapt the Hyperion Level 4 autonomous-driving platform for heavy-duty trucks.
The system will combine:
• Nvidia Hyperion for compute + sensors • Halos for safety architecture • Cosmos for edge-case data and synthetic training scenarios • Blackwell infrastructure for training, testing and refining Einride’s autonomous models
Einride will continue to develop and operate its own autonomous-driving stack, while Nvidia provides the underlying compute platform and AI development tools.
Einride currently operates hundreds of electric trucks across the U.S., Europe and Middle East, including autonomous trucks in customer deployments.
The company expects its fleet footprint to scale to 1,500-2,000 vehicles by 2028, with roughly 80% of that demand considered suitable for automation over the medium term.

item.title: @wallstengine: $MRVL TO SHOWCASE NEW 2NM OPTICAL TECHNOLOGY FOR AI DATA CENTERS Marvell says it will demonstrate s...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MRVL TO SHOWCASE NEW 2NM OPTICAL TECHNOLOGY FOR AI DATA CENTERS
Marvell says it will demonstrate several first-of-their-kind 2nm optical interconnect technologies at ECOC 2026 as AI networks move from 1.6T toward 3.2T connectivity.
The demos include:
• 2nm 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 • 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ with integrated MACsec • 2nm 1.6T ZR and coherent-lite O-band • 102.4T co-packaged optics platform using 200G-per-lane silicon photonics
The focus is higher bandwidth density and lower power per bit as hyperscalers connect increasingly large clusters of GPUs, CPUs, accelerators and memory.
Marvell says its CPO platform integrates optics directly with AI accelerators and switch silicon as copper reaches practical distance and power limits in large AI fabrics.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI-exposed jobs are seeing the largest pay growth in the US: Advertised pay in the most AI-exposed...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI-exposed jobs are seeing the largest pay growth in the US:
Advertised pay in the most AI-exposed occupations has surged +46% since the start of 2021.
At the same time, moderately AI-exposed jobs have seen +41% growth.
This compares to a +39% increase in all US posted wages and just +25% for the least AI-exposed jobs.
The gap began widening materially in mid-2025 and has continued to do so throughout this year.
The divergence suggests employers are increasingly competing for workers in AI-related occupations.
AI is reshaping the US compensation landscape.

Global gold ETF holdings are up to ~100 million ounces, near their highest level in at least 9 months.
Gold holdings have risen over +4 million ounces since their July low, more than recovering the decline recorded between April and July.
Most recently, gold-backed ETFs have seen 8 consecutive daily inflows, their longest streak since October 2025.
Meanwhile, gold prices moved roughly in-line with gold ETF holdings until mid-August this year.
Therefore, if gold prices catch up with the recent rise in holdings, they could surge above $5,000 in the coming months.
Investors are piling into gold funds at an accelerated pace.
